data.long_meaning: From the Roman name Lucia, derived from the Latin word lucere meaning 'to shine'. The name Lucianette is a feminine variant of the masculine name Lucian. The name Lucianette carries the meaning “Light, born from Lucy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Lucianette usually hope their child will grow to embody light, born from lucy and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Lucianetta
in_latin.long_meaning: Lucianetta nomen feminarum, quae originem habet a Luciano, santo qui veneratis, qui significat claritas, lux, et sapientia. In historia Ecclesiae, nominatur in tempore saeculi XV, in Italia, ubi nomen huiusmodi fuit in honorem sancta familiae.

historical_references.reference: Saint Lucianette of Quercy was a French virgin and hermit. She is said to have lived during the 11th century. According to legend, she was a noblewoman who renounced her wealth and married a poor farmer. When her husband died, she gave up her widow's veil and lived as a hermit in the forest. She was discovered by a hunter, who tried to abduct her. She forgave him and converted him to Christianity. He became her disciple, and they lived the rest of their lives together in the forest.

Saint Lucianette of Sens is a little-known French saint from the 15th century. She was a laywoman who lived in Sens, in France. According to legend, she was a wealthy widow who gave up her riches to live as a penitent in a cave. She was discovered by a group of robbers, who intended to rob her. They were converted to Christianity by her holiness and became her protectors. She was known for her charity and her miraculous healings.
